label: Tuesday, November 3, 2026 · Election Day edition
intro: Good morning. It's Tuesday, November 3rd. Here's your Read Daily brief.

items.title: Apple Beats Q4 Earnings Forecasts but Warns Rising Memory Costs Will Pressure Holiday Margins
items.take: Apple's first report under CEO John Ternus beat: $114.48B revenue, up 12%, and $2.10 EPS, with iPhone up 17% on the Duo and 18 Pro. The stock still sank 3% premarket Tuesday after holiday guidance of 45-46% gross margin versus 47.9% last quarter, with memory-chip inflation the stated culprit.

items.title: Apple's stock drops on weak margin forecast in Ternus' first earnings report
items.take: The headline numbers carried asterisks: EPS included a $0.05 tariff-refund benefit, wearables fell 8% to $8.3B and missed, and Greater China came in short of estimates. Services growth was guided at 8-9% versus 10.7% expected, and Ternus called the memory-price run unprecedented.

items.title: Stock Market Today: S&P 500, Nasdaq Rise After 3 Days of Losses; Dow Drops as Apple Sinks After Earnings
items.take: Stocks are rebounding on Election Day after three straight losing sessions, though the Dow lags as Apple sinks on that margin warning. Palantir fell more than 7% premarket despite solid earnings, on concerns over future bookings.

items.title: S&P futures muted, Nasdaq futures higher ahead of U.S. midterms
items.take: Futures hovered around the flatline as voters headed to the polls, with Deutsche Bank describing markets as caught between energy and AI themes. Analysts flag that a Democratic sweep could mean tougher AI rules and more resistance to data centers.

items.title: Apple Earnings, Midterms, Jobs Data Put Markets To The Test: 3 Charts To Watch This Week
items.take: Two tests remain after Apple: today's midterms and Friday's October jobs report, which shapes whether the Fed keeps a December rate hike on the table. Reports suggest Anthropic's IPO could come before Thanksgiving, with no date confirmed.

items.title: 'Ugly' Midterms, Increasing Your Nest Egg, Everywhere Millionaires
items.take: Today's rotation pick for election day: Surveillance on what an ugly midterm result means for markets, plus a practical segment on building the nest egg and the rise of everyday millionaires.
